run_id_note: run_id is when these files were last written. The directory name records the screening these tables belong to; re-running the same extractor over the same seed workbooks and the same baseline rewrites the files without making it a different screening.
candidate_sources: Chen 2023 ST18-ST20 forward and ST23 reverse
UKB Mapping 2025 sTables 31-34 forward and 35 reverse
Shin 2014: no metabolite-disease MR table extracted

bound_order.rule: A row is reordered only when its two extracted 95% bounds are both numeric and ci_low > ci_high, which no confidence interval can satisfy. Rows already in ascending order, rows with equal bounds and rows with a blank or non-numeric bound are written exactly as they were read.
bound_order.as_printed_note: Populated only on a reordered row, where they hold that row's bounds exactly as the source prints them; blank on every row that was not reordered.

extraction_rule: Keep a row only when the Excel row itself contains both a non-empty metabolite/exposure value and a non-empty disease/outcome value. Blank, footer, header, and placeholder cells are excluded; no pair is inferred from a paper title or from separate rows.
caveats: This is source extraction plus an anti-join, not scientific validation or acceptance of MR evidence.
Reverse and unresolved rows remain in the ledger but are excluded from new_pair_records.csv.
Phenotype terminology is preserved as printed in the source; disease/outcome interpretation remains a screening decision.

498 extracted UKB row(s) carry a shifted source layout. single-SNP Wald-ratio row: the printed 'Beta, Odds ratio, 95% UCI, 95% LCI, p value' header does not hold for this row. The odds ratio is one column right of the header, so the p value was read from column 10 and the 95% bounds, which are on the beta scale here, are carried in ci_low_beta_scale/ci_high_beta_scale rather than in ci_low/ci_high, which hold odds-ratio-scale bounds on every other row.

16944 extracted row(s) had their two 95% bounds reordered into numeric order. UKB rows: the printed header names column 11 '95% UCI' and column 12 '95% LCI', and the values are the other way round - column 11 holds the lower bound. Reading them under the header's own names yields ci_low > ci_high, which is impossible for a confidence interval. ci_low/ci_high therefore hold the two source numbers in numeric order, every reordered row says so in extraction_note, and the as-printed values are preserved in ci_low_as_printed/ci_high_as_printed. No bound was recomputed and no row whose bounds already ascend was touched.
Pair identity keeps '%': a ratio exposure such as 'Omega-3%' and the absolute exposure 'Omega-3' are two different exposures and are two different pairs.
